citation: Percy H. Sloan, photographer. Second Presbyterian Church of Chicago, Chicago, early 20th century ['Second Presbyterian Church, S. Michigan Ave., N.W. corner of 20th St.(?)' - photograph verso]. Newberry Library, Midwest MS Sloan, Box 1 Folder 25.
author: Percy H. Sloan
describes_date: between the 1901 rededication and the spire's loss in 1929
locator: The Prairie library's copy a19-nby-sloan-2ndpres-street (1269 x 1600 px), taken on Michigan Avenue's west walk north of the church, looking south.
rights_note: Newberry: 'makes its collections available for any lawful purpose, commercial or non-commercial, without licensing or permission fees to the library'.
note: The tower stands at the corner on 20th Street with an open belfry stage under a corbelled cornice and a tall slated spire with lucarnes; the east front's gable and great window stand behind it, the south flank and the hall's gable beyond. Read against the nave's 87'-8 1/4" ridge (HABS IL-328 sheet 4) the masonry stands about 38 m and the spire about 16 m more; the tower is nearer the camera than the gable, so both are upper figures.
what_it_supplies: the tower's stages and the spire's proportion over the masonry, as a reading against the HABS ridge height
that the church stands at the north-west corner of Michigan Avenue and 20th Street
what_it_does_not_supply: a measured height: the figures are proportions read in perspective
